output.population: Participants in 16 prospective cohort studies of grain intake and incident type 2 diabetes.
output.comparator: Lower intake, with dose-response estimates per 3 servings/day.
output.effect: Summary relative risk per 3 servings/day was 0.68 (95% CI 0.58 to 0.81; I2=82%; n=10) for whole grains and 0.95 (95% CI 0.88 to 1.04; I2=53%; n=6) for refined grains. Whole grains showed a nonlinear association (P nonlinearity <0.0001), whereas refined grains did not (P=0.10).
output.recommendation: The source supports replacing refined grains with whole grains and suggests at least two servings of whole grains per day to reduce type 2 diabetes risk.
output.applicability_boundary: Based on prospective cohort evidence; subtype findings were based on few studies and warrant further investigation, so causal certainty and specific food-subtype generalization are limited.
output.source_span: The summary relative risk per 3 servings per day was 0.68 for whole grains and 0.95 for refined grains.

uncertainties: Between-study heterogeneity was high for whole grains (I2=82%).
Specific whole-grain subtype findings were based on few studies.
